/-!
# Strong Papadimitriou–Ratajczak conjecture

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Greedy embedding § Planar graphs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greedy_embedding%23Planar_graphs)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [PR05] Papadimitriou, C. H. and Ratajczak, D., *On a conjecture related to geometric routing*,
  Theoret. Comput. Sci. 344 (2005), 3–14.
- [NP13] Nöllenburg, M. and Prutkin, R., *Euclidean greedy drawings of trees*, Proc. 21st European
  Symposium on Algorithms (ESA 2013). [arXiv:1306.5224](https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.5224)
- [NPR16] Nöllenburg, M., Prutkin, R. and Rutter, I., *On self-approaching and increasing-chord
  drawings of 3-connected planar graphs*, J. Comput. Geom. 7 (2016), 47–69.
  [arXiv:1409.0315](https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.0315)

A *greedy embedding* of a graph in the Euclidean plane assigns a point to every vertex so that
for every two distinct vertices $x \neq t$ some neighbour $y$ of $x$ is strictly closer to $t$
than $x$ is. Papadimitriou and Ratajczak [PR05] conjectured that every polyhedral graph
(3-connected planar graph, equivalently the graph of a convex polyhedron) has a greedy embedding
in the Euclidean plane; this was proved by Leighton–Moitra and by Angelini–Frati–Grilli.
The greedy embeddings produced by these proofs need not be planar drawings.

The *strong* Papadimitriou–Ratajczak conjecture, which remains open, asserts that every
polyhedral graph has a *convex greedy embedding*: a planar straight-line drawing that is greedy
and in which every face, including the outer face, is a convex polygon [PR05, NP13, NPR16].

## Formalisation choices

- Drawings are straight-line: a drawing is a map from the vertices to $\mathbb{R}^2$, and every
  edge is drawn as the closed segment between the images of its endpoints. This is the setting
  of greedy embeddings, where only the vertex positions matter.
- Mathlib has no notion of planar graph. Since every graph considered here is finite and simple,
  we use Fáry's theorem and call a graph planar if it admits a planar straight-line drawing,
  that is, a drawing with distinct vertex positions in which no vertex lies on a non-incident
  edge and two distinct edges meet only in common endpoints.
- The faces of a planar straight-line drawing are the connected components of the complement of
  the drawing in the plane. A bounded face is a convex polygon if it is a convex set. The
  unbounded outer face is a convex polygon if its complement, the closed region enclosed by the
  outer boundary, is a convex set.
-/
open scoped EuclideanGeometry
open SimpleGraph
namespace StrongPapadimitriouRatajczakConjecture
variable {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (p : V → ℝ²)

blocks.docstring:

justification.closest_existing_considered: SimpleGraph.UnitDistEmbedding / UnitDistanceEmbeddable (only vertex positions with unit-distance constraint, no geometric edge sets); segment ℝ (used as building block).
justification.name: StrongPapadimitriouRatajczakConjecture.drawing
justification.why_needed: The point set of a straight-line drawing (vertex points ∪ edge segments), needed to define faces as connected components of its complement. Nothing in Mathlib or the repo represents the plane set covered by a graph drawing.

def IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing : Prop :=
  Function.Injective p ∧
  (∀ u v w, G.Adj u v → p w ∈ segment ℝ (p u) (p v) → w = u ∨ w = v) ∧
  (∀ u v x y, G.Adj u v → G.Adj x y → s(u, v) ≠ s(x, y) →
    segment ℝ (p u) (p v) ∩ segment ℝ (p x) (p y) ⊆ p '' ({u, v} ∩ {x, y}))
blocks.docstring:
`p` is a planar straight-line drawing of `G`: distinct vertices are drawn at distinct points,
no vertex lies on the segment drawing an edge unless it is an endpoint of that edge, and the
segments drawing two distinct edges meet only in the images of their common endpoints.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Searched Mathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph and the repo for 'planar', 'drawing', 'crossing': only UnitDistance embeddings exist, which do not express crossing-freeness.
justification.name: StrongPapadimitriouRatajczakConjecture.IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing
justification.why_needed: Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib have no notion of planar graph, planar drawing, or edge crossing. Needed both for the 'planar' in 'polyhedral graph' and for the 'planar' in 'planar greedy drawing'.

blocks.name: IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing
blocks.text:
/-- `p` is a planar straight-line drawing of `G`: distinct vertices are drawn at distinct points,
no vertex lies on the segment drawing an edge unless it is an endpoint of that edge, and the
segments drawing two distinct edges meet only in the images of their common endpoints. -/
def IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing : Prop :=
  Function.Injective p ∧
  (∀ u v w, G.Adj u v → p w ∈ segment ℝ (p u) (p v) → w = u ∨ w = v) ∧
  (∀ u v x y, G.Adj u v → G.Adj x y → s(u, v) ≠ s(x, y) →
    segment ℝ (p u) (p v) ∩ segment ℝ (p x) (p y) ⊆ p '' ({u, v} ∩ {x, y}))

blocks.code:
def IsPolyhedral [Fintype V] : Prop :=
  G.IsKConnected 3 ∧ ∃ p : V → ℝ², IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing G p
blocks.docstring:
A finite simple graph is *polyhedral* if it is 3-connected and planar. By Steinitz's theorem
these are exactly the graphs of vertices and edges of convex polyhedra. Planarity is expressed,
via Fáry's theorem, as the existence of a planar straight-line drawing. Note that
`G.IsKConnected 3` requires more than three vertices.

justification.closest_existing_considered: SimpleGraph.IsKConnected (repo, used for 3-connectivity); no planarity primitive exists.
justification.name: StrongPapadimitriouRatajczakConjecture.IsPolyhedral
justification.why_needed: Polyhedral graph = 3-connected planar graph; no such definition exists.

blocks.name: IsPolyhedral
blocks.text:
/-- A finite simple graph is *polyhedral* if it is 3-connected and planar. By Steinitz's theorem
these are exactly the graphs of vertices and edges of convex polyhedra. Planarity is expressed,
via Fáry's theorem, as the existence of a planar straight-line drawing. Note that
`G.IsKConnected 3` requires more than three vertices. -/
def IsPolyhedral [Fintype V] : Prop :=
  G.IsKConnected 3 ∧ ∃ p : V → ℝ², IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing G p

blocks.code:
def IsGreedy : Prop :=
  ∀ x t, x ≠ t → ∃ y, G.Adj x y ∧ dist (p y) (p t) < dist (p x) (p t)
blocks.docstring:
The vertex positions `p` form a *greedy embedding* of `G` in the Euclidean plane: for every
two distinct vertices $x \neq t$ there is a neighbour $y$ of $x$ with $d(y, t) < d(x, t)$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Repo `greedySidon` (unrelated); Mathlib SimpleGraph.dist (graph metric, not Euclidean).
justification.name: StrongPapadimitriouRatajczakConjecture.IsGreedy
justification.why_needed: Greedy embedding (distance-decreasing neighbour for every pair of distinct vertices) does not exist in Mathlib or the repo.

blocks.name: IsGreedy
blocks.text:
/-- The vertex positions `p` form a *greedy embedding* of `G` in the Euclidean plane: for every
two distinct vertices $x \neq t$ there is a neighbour $y$ of $x$ with $d(y, t) < d(x, t)$. -/
def IsGreedy : Prop :=
  ∀ x t, x ≠ t → ∃ y, G.Adj x y ∧ dist (p y) (p t) < dist (p x) (p t)

def HasConvexFaces : Prop :=
  ∀ x ∉ drawing G p,
    (Bornology.IsBounded (connectedComponentIn (drawing G p)ᶜ x) →
      Convex ℝ (connectedComponentIn (drawing G p)ᶜ x)) ∧
    (¬ Bornology.IsBounded (connectedComponentIn (drawing G p)ᶜ x) →
      Convex ℝ (connectedComponentIn (drawing G p)ᶜ x)ᶜ)
blocks.docstring:
Every face of the drawing of `G` with vertex positions `p` is a convex polygon. The faces are
the connected components of the complement of the drawing. A bounded face is required to be a
convex set; the unbounded (outer) face is required to have convex complement, i.e. the closed
region enclosed by the outer boundary is convex.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Convex ℝ, connectedComponentIn, Bornology.IsBounded (all used); no face notion exists.
justification.name: StrongPapadimitriouRatajczakConjecture.HasConvexFaces
justification.why_needed: Faces of a plane drawing and their convexity are not available anywhere; defined via connectedComponentIn of the complement of the drawing, Bornology.IsBounded and Convex ℝ.

blocks.name: HasConvexFaces
blocks.text:
/-- Every face of the drawing of `G` with vertex positions `p` is a convex polygon. The faces are
the connected components of the complement of the drawing. A bounded face is required to be a
convex set; the unbounded (outer) face is required to have convex complement, i.e. the closed
region enclosed by the outer boundary is convex. -/
def HasConvexFaces : Prop :=
  ∀ x ∉ drawing G p,
    (Bornology.IsBounded (connectedComponentIn (drawing G p)ᶜ x) →
      Convex ℝ (connectedComponentIn (drawing G p)ᶜ x)) ∧
    (¬ Bornology.IsBounded (connectedComponentIn (drawing G p)ᶜ x) →
      Convex ℝ (connectedComponentIn (drawing G p)ᶜ x)ᶜ)

blocks.code:
def IsConvexGreedyEmbedding : Prop :=
  IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing G p ∧ HasConvexFaces G p ∧ IsGreedy G p
blocks.docstring:
`p` is a *convex greedy embedding* of `G`: a planar straight-line drawing of `G` in which
every face (including the outer face) is a convex polygon and which is greedy.

justification.name: StrongPapadimitriouRatajczakConjecture.IsConvexGreedyEmbedding
justification.why_needed: Bundles the three conditions (planar straight-line drawing, convex faces, greedy) that constitute a 'convex greedy embedding' so the theorem statement mirrors the informal statement.

/-- `p` is a *convex greedy embedding* of `G`: a planar straight-line drawing of `G` in which

@[category API, AMS 5 52]
theorem IsGreedy.injective {G : SimpleGraph V} {p : V → ℝ²} (h : IsGreedy G p) :
    Function.Injective p := by
  intro x t hxt
  by_contra hne
  obtain ⟨y, -, hy⟩ := h x t hne
  rw [hxt, _root_.dist_self] at hy
  exact absurd hy (not_lt.mpr dist_nonneg)
blocks.docstring: A greedy embedding places distinct vertices at distinct points.

claims.decomposer_note: Single universal Prop: for every finite simple 3-connected planar graph G (polyhedral graph, equivalently by Steinitz the 1-skeleton of a convex polyhedron, so ≥ 4 vertices) there exists a straight-line drawing in the Euclidean plane ℝ² with distinct vertex positions that is (a) greedy — for every pair of distinct vertices x ≠ t some neighbor y of x satisfies strict d(y,t) < d(x,t) (Euclidean metric) — and (b) planar (no edge crossings) with every face, including the outer face, a convex polygon ('convex greedy embedding' = 'planar greedy drawing with convex faces' in Nöllenburg–Prutkin 2013 and Nöllenburg–Prutkin–Rutter 2016); the article's weak form (greedy embedding without planarity/convexity, proved by Leighton–Moitra and Angelini–Frati–Grilli) is background only and not posed by the statement.
claims.reviewer_why: c07's declaration (lightly edited) is used: polyhedral = finite simple graph with the repo's `SimpleGraph.IsKConnected 3` (forces >3 vertices) and Fáry-planarity (existence of an injective, crossing-free straight-line drawing); conclusion = ∃ p : V → ℝ² that is a planar straight-line drawing, has all faces (connected components of the complement of the drawing) convex — bounded faces convex sets, the outer face with convex complement (i.e. convex outer polygon) — and is greedy (∀ x ≠ t, ∃ neighbour y with strict Euclidean dist (p y) (p t) < dist (p x) (p t)). This matches the source reading 'planar greedy drawing with convex faces' (NP13, NPR16). Edits: qualified `_root_.dist_self` (name clash with `SimpleGraph.dist_self` under `open SimpleGraph`), added the `IsGreedy.injective` API lemma from c08/c05, added AMS 68, tightened the module docstring. c02/c05/c08 are equivalent alternatives; c01/c03/c04 are faithful but use bespoke 3-connectivity and less transparent frontier/convex-hull characterisations of convex faces; c06 is rejected because its planar-drawing predicate is unsatisfiable for any graph with an edge (verified in Lean), making its theorem vacuously true.
claims.source_text: every polyhedral graph has a convex greedy embedding
claims.text_span: every polyhedral graph has a convex greedy embedding

context:
In distributed computing and geometric graph theory, greedy embedding is a process of assigning coordinates to the nodes of a telecommunications network in order to allow greedy geographic routing to be used to route messages within the network. Although greedy embedding has been proposed for use in wireless sensor networks, in which the nodes already have positions in physical space, these existing positions may differ from the positions given to them by greedy embedding, which may in some cases be points in a virtual space of a higher dimension, or in a non-Euclidean geometry. In this sense, greedy embedding may be viewed as a form of graph drawing, in which an abstract graph (the communications network) is embedded into a geometric space.
The idea of performing geographic routing using coordinates in a virtual space, instead of using physical coordinates, is due to Rao et al. Subsequent developments have shown that every network has a greedy embedding with succinct vertex coordinates in the hyperbolic plane, that certain graphs including the polyhedral graphs have greedy embeddings in the Euclidean plane, and that unit disk graphs have greedy embeddings in Euclidean spaces of moderate dimensions with low stretch factors.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The single-slot decomposition matches the statement; the notes' reading (3-connected planar finite simple graph; straight-line drawing; strict greedy condition; planar with all faces including the outer face convex; weak form is background only) was followed exactly.

open scoped EuclideanGeometry
open SimpleGraph

namespace StrongPapadimitriouRatajczakConjecture

variable {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (p : V → ℝ²)

/-- The set of points of the plane covered by the straight-line drawing of `G` with vertex
positions `p`: the vertex points together with the closed segment joining the endpoints of every
edge. -/
def drawing : Set ℝ² :=
  Set.range p ∪ ⋃ (u : V) (v : V) (_ : G.Adj u v), segment ℝ (p u) (p v)

/-- `p` is a planar straight-line drawing of `G`: distinct vertices are drawn at distinct points,
no vertex lies on the segment drawing an edge unless it is an endpoint of that edge, and the
segments drawing two distinct edges meet only in the images of their common endpoints. -/
def IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing : Prop :=
  Function.Injective p ∧
  (∀ u v w, G.Adj u v → p w ∈ segment ℝ (p u) (p v) → w = u ∨ w = v) ∧
  (∀ u v x y, G.Adj u v → G.Adj x y → s(u, v) ≠ s(x, y) →
    segment ℝ (p u) (p v) ∩ segment ℝ (p x) (p y) ⊆ p '' ({u, v} ∩ {x, y}))

/-- A finite simple graph is *polyhedral* if it is 3-connected and planar. By Steinitz's theorem
these are exactly the graphs of vertices and edges of convex polyhedra. Planarity is expressed,
via Fáry's theorem, as the existence of a planar straight-line drawing. Note that
`G.IsKConnected 3` requires more than three vertices. -/
def IsPolyhedral [Fintype V] : Prop :=
  G.IsKConnected 3 ∧ ∃ p : V → ℝ², IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing G p

/-- The vertex positions `p` form a *greedy embedding* of `G` in the Euclidean plane: for every
two distinct vertices $x \neq t$ there is a neighbour $y$ of $x$ with $d(y, t) < d(x, t)$. -/
def IsGreedy : Prop :=
  ∀ x t, x ≠ t → ∃ y, G.Adj x y ∧ dist (p y) (p t) < dist (p x) (p t)

/-- Every face of the drawing of `G` with vertex positions `p` is a convex polygon. The faces are
the connected components of the complement of the drawing. A bounded face is required to be a
convex set; the unbounded (outer) face is required to have convex complement, i.e. the closed
region enclosed by the outer boundary is convex. -/
def HasConvexFaces : Prop :=
  ∀ x ∉ drawing G p,
    (Bornology.IsBounded (connectedComponentIn (drawing G p)ᶜ x) →
      Convex ℝ (connectedComponentIn (drawing G p)ᶜ x)) ∧
    (¬ Bornology.IsBounded (connectedComponentIn (drawing G p)ᶜ x) →
      Convex ℝ (connectedComponentIn (drawing G p)ᶜ x)ᶜ)

/-- `p` is a *convex greedy embedding* of `G`: a planar straight-line drawing of `G` in which
every face (including the outer face) is a convex polygon and which is greedy. -/
def IsConvexGreedyEmbedding : Prop :=
  IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing G p ∧ HasConvexFaces G p ∧ IsGreedy G p

/-- A greedy embedding of the complete graph is given by any injective vertex placement. -/
@[category test, AMS 5 52]
theorem isGreedy_top (hp : Function.Injective p) : IsGreedy (⊤ : SimpleGraph V) p := by
  intro x t hxt
  exact ⟨t, hxt, by simpa using dist_pos.mpr (hp.ne hxt)⟩

/-- The empty graph on at least two vertices has no greedy embedding. -/
@[category test, AMS 5 52]
theorem not_isGreedy_bot [Nontrivial V] : ¬ IsGreedy (⊥ : SimpleGraph V) p := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨x, t, hxt⟩ := exists_pair_ne V
  obtain ⟨y, hy, -⟩ := h x t hxt
  exact hy

/-- A greedy embedding places distinct vertices at distinct points. -/
@[category API, AMS 5 52]
theorem IsGreedy.injective {G : SimpleGraph V} {p : V → ℝ²} (h : IsGreedy G p) :
    Function.Injective p := by
  intro x t hxt
  by_contra hne
  obtain ⟨y, -, hy⟩ := h x t hne
  rw [hxt, _root_.dist_self] at hy
  exact absurd hy (not_lt.mpr dist_nonneg)

/-- Any injective vertex placement is a planar straight-line drawing of the empty graph. -/
@[category test, AMS 5 52]
theorem isPlanarStraightLineDrawing_bot (hp : Function.Injective p) :
    IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing (⊥ : SimpleGraph V) p :=
  ⟨hp, fun _ _ _ h => h.elim, fun _ _ _ _ h => h.elim⟩

/-- A graph on at most three vertices is not polyhedral. -/
@[category test, AMS 5 52]
theorem not_isPolyhedral_of_card_le [Fintype V] (h : Fintype.card V ≤ 3) : ¬ IsPolyhedral G :=
  fun hG => not_isKConnected_of_card_le h hG.1

/-- **Strong Papadimitriou–Ratajczak conjecture** [PR05]. Every polyhedral graph, i.e. every
finite simple 3-connected planar graph, has a convex greedy embedding in the Euclidean plane:
a planar straight-line drawing in which every face (including the outer face) is a convex
polygon and such that for every two distinct vertices $x \neq t$ some neighbour $y$ of $x$
satisfies $d(y, t) < d(x, t)$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5 52 68]
theorem strong_papadimitriou_ratajczak_conjecture [Fintype V] (hG : IsPolyhedral G) :
    ∃ p : V → ℝ², IsConvexGreedyEmbedding G p := by
  sorry

end StrongPapadimitriouRatajczakConjecture

items: Planarity: Mathlib has no planar-graph notion. Since all graphs here are finite and simple, planarity is defined via Fáry's theorem as the existence of a planar straight-line drawing (injective vertex positions, no vertex on a non-incident edge segment, two distinct edges meet only in the images of their common endpoints). A reviewer should confirm this equivalent characterisation is acceptable as the definition of 'planar'.

Polyhedral graph = 3-connected ∧ planar, using the existing `SimpleGraph.IsKConnected G 3` (which requires 3 < card V, i.e. ≥ 4 vertices, and connectivity after deleting any < 3 vertices). Steinitz's equivalent characterisation (1-skeleton of a convex polyhedron) is only mentioned in the docstring.

Drawings are straight-line (edges = closed segments between vertex images), following Nöllenburg–Prutkin(–Rutter) where all drawings are straight-line with distinct vertex points; greedy embeddings are determined by vertex positions alone.

Faces are the connected components (`connectedComponentIn`) of the complement of the drawing (union of vertex points and edge segments). 'Every face is a convex polygon' is formalised as: each bounded face is a convex set, and the unbounded (outer) face has convex complement (i.e. the closed region enclosed by the outer boundary is convex). Convexity is non-strict (180° angles allowed), as in Tutte's convex drawings; the sources say 'convex', not 'strictly convex'.

Greedy: for every ordered pair of distinct vertices x ≠ t there is a neighbour y of x with strict inequality dist (p y) (p t) < dist (p x) (p t), Euclidean metric on `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)` (repo notation ℝ²).
The order of conjuncts in IsConvexGreedyEmbedding is planar drawing ∧ convex faces ∧ greedy; the theorem quantifies existentially over p after the polyhedral hypothesis.

Bespoke definitions live in the problem file (inside the namespace) because the task restricts writing to a single candidate file; in a real PR the generic ones (drawing, IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing, IsGreedy, HasConvexFaces) could move to FormalConjecturesForMathlib.

Four short `category test` lemmas exercise the new definitions (complete graph with injective placement is greedy; empty graph on ≥ 2 vertices is not greedy; any injective placement is a planar straight-line drawing of the empty graph; graphs on ≤ 3 vertices are not polyhedral).

reviewer_notes: Ambiguities in the original one-line statement, resolved following the Wikipedia article and NP13/NPR16: (1) 'polyhedral graph' = finite simple 3-connected planar graph (Steinitz); (2) 'convex greedy embedding' = planar straight-line greedy drawing in which every face, including the outer face, is a convex polygon; (3) convexity is non-strict (angles of π allowed), as 'convex' rather than 'strictly convex' is what the sources say; (4) planarity of the abstract graph is encoded via Fáry's theorem (existence of a crossing-free straight-line drawing) because Mathlib has no planar-graph notion — a reviewer should confirm accepting this characterisation. Faces are modeled as connected components of ℝ² minus the drawing; for a plane drawing of a 3-connected graph these are exactly the polygonal faces, and 'outer face is a convex polygon' is encoded as convexity of its complement (the closed region enclosed by the outer cycle). Candidate c06 is unfaithful: its non-crossing condition is quantified over all pairs of edges without requiring them to be distinct, so a single edge segment must be contained in its two endpoint images — impossible; I verified in Lean that `IsPlanarDrawing G p ∧ G.Adj u v → False`, so its hypothesis is unsatisfiable and its theorem vacuous. All other candidates were faithful; differences were stylistic (bespoke vs repo 3-connectivity, frontier-based vs set-convexity face conditions). Final file compiles with only the `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning.
